edition: Issue 046: The new 007 is a former vampire, a Kiwi golfer wins the season-long spreadsheet, and the FMA's top table is suddenly a lot less crowded
tagline: Your 3-minute Tuesday reset: a new Bond anointed by the warehouse, a very Kiwi path to the PGA Tour, and the markets watchdog's increasingly empty boardroom.

stories.headline: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond — Amazon MGM's first 007 and the end of the longest wait in spy history
stories.summary: Robert Pattinson, 40, is the seventh actor to play James Bond in the official series, replacing Daniel Craig for the untitled 26th film - Denis Villeneuve directing, Steven Knight writing, Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing - in the franchise's first Amazon MGM Studios outing, announced five years after No Time to Die in the longest hiatus in 007 history.

body.text: The announcement the internet has debated since Daniel Craig hung up the licence: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond. He becomes the seventh actor to play 007 in the official film series, and the first since 1962's Dr No not handpicked by a Broccoli - Bond 26 is the franchise's first Amazon MGM Studios production after Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson relinquished creative control in 2025 (Amazon bought MGM for US$8.5 billion in 2022). The still-untitled film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve (Dune), written by Steven Knight (Peaky Blinders) and produced by Amy Pascal and David Heyman, with no release date set though shooting is expected to start next year. The reveal - teased by wiping the official 007 accounts and posting a repeating 'Identity confirmed' - ends the longest gap between Bonds in the franchise's history, five years since No Time to Die in 2021. Pattinson, 40, on the older side to begin as 007 and currently mid-shoot on The Batman Part II, reportedly beat screen-test finalists Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Nicholas Hoult for a role in a series that has grossed more than US$7 billion at the box office.

Right, the obvious jokes first: for a franchise built on shaken not stirred, the world's worst-kept casting secret was confirmed by the 007 social accounts wiping their entire history and typing 'Identity confirmed' like a teenager announcing a rebrand. We were already past identity confirmation - the internet has been confirming this for years. Pattinson is the first Bond in six decades not handpicked by a Broccoli; he's been handpicked by a warehouse. Amazon spent $8.5 billion to own the tuxedo and reportedly signed the world's busiest bat for the gig, so one man now carries two iconic franchises, one of which fakes its hero's death every few years and the other - well, same energy, just with fewer gadgets. Silver lining: at 40, Pattinson is finally old enough to order the drink the whole franchise is named after without being carded, which is honestly the most Bond arc any of us could have asked for. Welcome to the machine, Rob. The last guy got a funeral and a title card promising he'll return, so at least you know what the company town expects.

Amazon MGM Studios / official 007 social accounts (16 Nov 2026, 'Identity confirmed' announcement): Robert Pattinson is the seventh actor to play James Bond in the official series, succeeding Daniel Craig; Bond 26 is directed by Denis Villeneuve from a script by Steven Knight, produced by Amy Pascal and David Heyman for Amazon MGM Studios. AP via Seattle Times / Daily Herald (16 Nov 2026, Jake Coyle): the naming ends the longest hiatus in Bond history, five years after No Time to Die (2021) - the first Bond film whose story concluded with the character's death; Pattinson (40) is relatively old to begin as 007 and is in production on The Batman Part II; other finalists who screen-tested in late October were Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Nicholas Hoult; Amazon bought MGM for US$8.5 billion in 2022 and Broccoli and Wilson relinquished creative control of 007 in 2025, making Bond 26 the first official Bond film since Dr No (1962) not handpicked by a Broccoli; Bond films have grossed more than US$7 billion worldwide; Puck reported Pattinson is signed to a three-movie deal. Irish Times / Guardian (16 Nov 2026, Andrew Pulver and Catherine Shoard): all earlier content was wiped from 007's X and Instagram accounts before the announcement; Pattinson said being entrusted with 007 was 'the honour of a lifetime'. Stuff (16 Nov 2026, breaking): Pattinson named the 7th Bond, taking over from Daniel Craig.

stories.headline: Kiwi golfer Daniel Hillier books a PGA Tour card for next season — 10th in the Race to Dubai will do it
stories.summary: Daniel Hillier will play on the PGA Tour next season after finishing in a share of 19th at the DP World Tour Championship and 10th on the Race to Dubai standings - cards go to the top 10 eligible players - joining compatriot Ryan Fox, while Rory McIlroy won a record-equalling order of merit and broke down dedicating it to his father.

body.text: Kiwi golfer Daniel Hillier is going to America. Hillier secured his PGA Tour card for next season after finishing in a share of 19th at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai and 10th on the Race to Dubai season standings - the tour issues cards to the top 10 eligible players at season's end. He will join compatriot Ryan Fox on the world's biggest tour. The same week in Dubai delivered the year's most human moment in sport: Rory McIlroy won a record-equalling order of merit crown, edging Eugenio Chacarra in the Tour Championship, then broke down in tears dedicating the win to his father Gerry, 68, who underwent a double-lung transplant in September. 'He told me, Go and win the Race to Dubai for me, so this is for him,' McIlroy said, his voice cracking.

Let's talk about golf maths, because only golf can make 'finish 19th' sound like a triumph: Hillier finished 10th in a season-long spreadsheet that runs from Abu Dhabi to the other side of the planet, and the door to the richest tour on earth swings open. If our KiwiSaver balances worked on Race to Dubai rules we would all be retired millionaires, which tells you everything about which spreadsheet actually pays out. Either way, two Kiwis on the PGA Tour next season means two of us voluntarily wrecking our sleep to watch golf from the other side of the world - a decision we will complain about loudly and at length. And the most tear-jerking scene of the week belonged to nobody's highlight reel: Rory McIlroy sobbing into the mic about his dad's double-lung transplant and the promise made from a hospital bed. Tissues out, banter hold - that one's on the house.

Stuff (17 Nov 2026, Kiwi golfer Daniel Hillier secures PGA Tour card): Hillier will play on the PGA Tour next season, joining compatriot Ryan Fox, after finishing in a share of 19th at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai (played 15 Nov at Jumeirah Golf Estates) and 10th on the Race to Dubai season standings; PGA Tour cards are issued to the top 10 eligible players at the end of the season. Same report: Rory McIlroy won a record-equalling order of merit crown after a tense battle with Eugenio Chacarra in the DP World Tour Championship, dedicating the win to his father Gerry, 68, who underwent a double-lung transplant in September - 'He told me, Go and win the Race to Dubai for me, so this is for him.'

stories.headline: FMA's great escape: deputy chairman is the third top-brass exit as workplace-conduct investigation grinds on
stories.summary: Financial Markets Authority deputy chairman Steven Bardy is resigning three months before his term ends - the third senior exit in about a year, alongside chairman Craig Stobo (now due to become a New Zealand First MP) and chief executive Samantha Barrass - as an MBIE-commissioned investigation into workplace culture draws contributions from more than 80 past and present staff.

body.text: The Financial Markets Authority is running out of top brass. Deputy chairman Steven Bardy has resigned - he wrote to Commerce and Consumer Affairs Minister Cameron Brewer on 12 November to stand down on 20 November, three months before his term ends - the latest exit from the markets watchdog as an investigation into its workplace culture and conduct continues. Bardy is the third senior figure out in roughly a year: chairman Craig Stobo resigned in May after being found to have made too many political statements for an apolitical role (he is now due to become a New Zealand First MP), and chief executive Samantha Barrass resigned in September amid an investigation into her employment. Board member Prasanna Gai had already resigned in December before the end of his term. The wider workplace investigation - commissioned by MBIE and led by Kristy McDonald KC after allegations of bullying and toxic behaviour at the FMA's upper echelons became public - is understood to have drawn contributions from more than 80 past and present staff. Bardy, who joined the board in 2022 and served as acting chairman during the early turmoil, told the minister he is 'excited at what lies ahead for the FMA under James' leadership'; current chairman James Miller, appointed in August, called Bardy's service 'significant and valuable' during a 'challenging period'.

Quick headcount, because the FMA's top table is becoming a game of musical chairs where the music stopped in December: chairman resigned in May - for making too many political statements in an apolitical role, which is the regulatory equivalent of getting fired from the library for talking too loudly, except this chairman resigned and is now, wait for it, due to become a New Zealand First MP. Chief executive resigned in September. Deputy chairman handed in his letter this month, after politely waiting until after the election, because nothing says independence quite like scheduling your resignation around the political cycle. The FMA's entire job is deciding whether everyone else's finances are fair, decent and orderly - and its own leadership has looked like anything but. To be crystal clear: none of that is a joke about the actual workplace investigation into bullying and toxic behaviour that has pulled in more than 80 current and former staff. That is real, and nobody here is laughing at it. We are only noting that when the conduct cop burns through its own brass like this, somewhere a very patient mailroom worker is quietly wondering whether the exit-interview forms have already been printed.

NZ Herald (16 Nov 2026, Jenée Tibshraeny, FMA deputy chairman Steven Bardy resigns, after resignation of chairman, chief executive): Bardy wrote to Commerce and Consumer Affairs Minister Cameron Brewer on 12 November advising he will stand down on 20 November, three months before his term ends; he had told chairman James Miller in recent months he intended to resign but did not want to do so until after the general election; Bardy served as acting chairman from December (2025) when Craig Stobo stood aside pending a conduct investigation; Stobo was found to have made too many political statements for an apolitical role, resigned in May, and is now due to become a New Zealand First MP; chief executive Samantha Barrass resigned in September amid an investigation into her employment, which was subsumed by a wider workplace investigation begun after allegations of bullying and toxic behaviour at the upper echelons of the FMA became public; the investigation is commissioned by MBIE, led by Kristy McDonald KC, and more than 80 past and present staff are understood to have contributed; board member Prasanna Gai resigned in December before the end of his term; Bardy joined the FMA board in 2022.
